reasons: The file is short and simple, so there is little to break, but it cannot be confirmed to work from this file alone.

terms.meaning: A group of web addresses the app answers, which can be attached to the main server as one unit.
Add a group of routes to the app so the app answers them.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and the router
sections.what: Brings in the web framework and the health routes, and creates an empty router.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: use
sections.title: Attaches the health routes
sections.what: Adds the health routes to the router and exports it for the server to use.
sections.why: Likely reason: groups routes by area, so each new area is added as one line here.
sections.watch_out: A route file that is not attached here never has its routes run.

summary: Gathers the route groups into one router that the server can use.
purpose: Gives the server one place to attach route groups.
why: Likely reason: keeps the list of route groups short and easy to extend. Not stated in the code.
how: Creates a router, attaches the health routes to it, and exports the router.
outputs: A router the server can attach to the app.
risks: Only health routes are attached here. The main route file routes.ts is attached elsewhere, so a reader of this file alone would think the app has no other routes.
debug: If a route returns 404, check whether its router is attached in this file or in the file that registers routes.ts. The server start-up file is not in this packet.
